intro: To open Notion links in browser on Mac, turn on Open Notion links in browser in the Notion desktop app under Settings > Preferences. Then, in Notion on the web, turn off Open links in desktop app, because the two settings are meant to work as a pair.
tldr: Open the Notion desktop app, go to Settings > Preferences, and turn on Open Notion links in browser.
In Notion on the web, go to Settings > Preferences and turn off Open links in desktop app.
If links still open the Mac app, check the web switch first, then refresh with ⌘R and test a fresh link.
Notion's help documents only ⌘R and ⌘⇧R, and both refresh the app. Neither one changes link routing.

blocks.text: Notion has two link settings, and each one lives in a different app. The first sits in the Notion desktop app on your Mac. The second sits in Notion on the web, in your browser. Each setting tells Notion where to send a link when you click it. Change only one, and links can keep opening in the Mac app. Set both, and the routing stays predictable.
Why the two settings have to match

Notion's help pages say the two toggles are meant to be used as a pair. Open Notion links in browser is the desktop app setting. Open links in desktop app is the web setting. For browser routing, the first one must be on and the second one must be off. The web setting also needs the desktop app installed before it can do anything. That is why changing only one switch often fails.

blocks.text: Set the desktop app to open links in the browser

Open the Notion desktop app and look at the sidebar. Click the down arrow next to your workspace name. Choose Settings, then Preferences. Scroll to Desktop app settings. Turn on Open Notion links in browser. From then on, Notion sends links to your browser. Notion's account settings page describes this exact route, so the path is documented, not guessed.
Turn off the web setting in Notion on the web

Open Notion in your browser and sign in to the same account you use in the Mac app. Go to Settings > Preferences. Find Open links in desktop app and turn it off. If that switch stays on, links can still route into the app, even after you changed the desktop setting. Check the web switch first when a link misbehaves, because it is easy to miss.
A worked example: a link from a colleague

Say a colleague posts a Notion page link in a chat on your Mac. You want it to open in your browser, because your research tabs live there. Before you click, check the desktop switch. Then check the web switch. Click the link. If the browser tab shows the page, both switches are set correctly.

If the Mac app opens instead, the web switch is the likely cause. It is the one people forget, because it lives in a different app. Turn it off, quit the Notion desktop app, open it again, and click a link you have not opened yet. Expect old behavior to linger in links you already opened this session, so test with a fresh one.
Open one link in the browser or the Mac app

Notion's help documents one per-link move, and it goes the other direction. If a link does not open in the Mac app, open it in the browser. Click ••• at the top right, open More, scroll to the bottom of the menu, and choose Open in Mac app. Notion does not document a matching per-link step that sends a link from the Mac app to the browser. For browser routing, use the two settings instead.
Mistakes that keep links opening in the app

items: Changing only the desktop setting and leaving the web setting on.
Changing the setting in the browser when you meant the Mac app. Each setting lives in its own app.
Turning on the web setting before the desktop app is installed. The web setting needs the app.
Signing in to a different account or workspace in the web app than the one in the Mac app.
Waiting for a shortcut to switch routing. Notion's help pages list none for this.

blocks.text: Check your Mac app version before you start

Notion's help pages do not name a minimum Mac app version for the link toggles. The desktop beta page does name one. It says to update to version 7.39.0 or later before you join the desktop beta. To check your build, open the Notion menu and choose Check for Updates. Installing an update is a sensible first move when a setting looks missing.

A third-party tracker, Releasebot, lists Mac builds v7.42.1 and v7.42.3, both dated Nov 4, 2026. Releasebot is not Notion, so treat its list as a hint, not proof. It says links to organization settings and creator profiles now open in the browser. It does not say the same is true for ordinary page links, and Notion's own pages did not confirm it.

Do not confuse the Mac app build with Notion's product release numbers. Notion 3.8, titled Context for your agents, is dated Oct 13, 2026 on Notion's releases page. It is a product release, not a Mac app build number. Notion 3.7 is dated Sep 15, 2026 on the same page.
What the keyboard shortcuts do and do not change

Notion's help pages list two shortcuts that matter here, and both refresh rather than route. Press ⌘R to refresh Notion on Mac. The help page ties it to new features. Press ⌘⇧R during the desktop beta to refresh the client itself, which helps when the beta toggle is missing. Neither shortcut changes where links open. No ⌥ or ⌃ shortcut for link routing appeared in the help pages reviewed for this guide.
Troubleshooting when a link still opens in the app

Work through the checks in this order. Start with the two switches, because they cause most of the trouble. Then refresh the app. Then test a link you have not clicked yet in this session, so you can tell a new result from an old one.
When Notion keeps launching at login

Notion's help says device-level settings may override Notion settings when the desktop app keeps launching by itself. The steps on that page cover Windows startup settings. They do not give Mac steps. This guide therefore cannot give you a verified Mac menu path for that problem. Check your Mac's own login settings. If the app still opens, contact Notion support and include your app version.

blocks.title: Version caveat
blocks.text: The macOS 13 minimum that some third-party sites list is not confirmed by Notion's help. Notion's download page does not state a minimum macOS version either, so that requirement stays unverified here.
Test that the setting worked

Find a Notion link in an email, a chat, or a document. Click it without refreshing first. If a browser tab opens and shows the page, the setting works. If the Mac app opens instead, go back and check both switches. If the switches look right but the app still wins, press ⌘R in the Mac app and try a new link.
Why you might want browser links at all

Some people want Notion links in the browser they already use, with the tabs and sign-ins they already keep there. Others prefer the Mac app for pages they open all day, and only want the browser for outside links. Neither choice is wrong. Pick the setting that matches your work, then use it for a week before you judge it.

If you mostly work inside Notion, the desktop app suits you. If you jump between Notion and other web tools all day, the browser may suit you better. Both settings are on or off switches, so you can change your mind at any time.
Next steps for Notion on Mac

Once links route the way you want, the next question is usually about Notion itself. [Notion on Mac](/apps/notion) covers voice help for pages, shortcuts, and drafts. Notion's own help center is the place to confirm settings when menus change between versions.

faq.question: Can I send just one page to the browser instead of the Mac app?
faq.answer: Notion's help does not document a per-link setting that sends a link to the browser. The documented per-link step goes the other way. Open the link in the browser, click ••• at the top right, open More, and choose Open in Mac app at the bottom of the menu. For browser routing across all links, use the two settings.

faq.question: Do I need the Notion desktop app for this to work?
faq.answer: Yes. The web setting, Open links in desktop app, needs the desktop app installed, and the desktop setting must be off before it works. For browser routing, the desktop app still holds the first switch, so install it from Notion's download page before you start.

faq.question: Why do links still open in the Mac app after I changed the setting?
faq.answer: The most common cause is the web switch. If Open links in desktop app stays on in Notion on the web, links can still go to the app. Turn it off, then click a link you have not opened yet. Also confirm you changed the desktop setting in the desktop app, not in the browser.

faq.question: Does ⌘R change where Notion links open?
faq.answer: No. Notion's help documents ⌘R as a refresh shortcut on Mac, tied to new features. It does not change link routing. Refresh after you change settings if links still misbehave, then test with a new link.

faq.question: Which Mac app version do I need for these link settings?
faq.answer: Notion's help pages name no minimum Mac app version for the link toggles. The desktop beta requires version 7.39.0 or later. Releasebot, a third-party tracker, lists v7.42.3 dated Nov 4, 2026. Check your own build under the Notion menu, then Check for Updates.

faq.question: Is Notion 3.8 the version of my Mac app?
faq.answer: No. Notion 3.8, dated Oct 13, 2026, is a product release on Notion's releases page. Mac app builds have their own version numbers, such as 7.42.3 in the Releasebot feed. Compare the build number in your app with the build numbers, not the product release.

faq.question: Does this guide cover Windows too?
faq.answer: No. This guide covers the Mac app only. Notion's help page for desktop covers both Mac and Windows, so check that page if you use Windows.

steps.name: Open the Notion desktop app
steps.text: Start the Notion desktop app on your Mac. If you only use Notion in a browser tab, install the desktop app first from Notion's download page. The page offers separate Mac builds: Universal, Apple Silicon, and Intel x64. The Universal build is the default button, and it is the safe pick if you are not sure which chip your Mac uses.
steps.tip: Pick Universal if you are unsure. Notion lists it as the default button on the download page.

steps.name: Open Settings > Preferences in the sidebar
steps.text: In the sidebar, click the down arrow next to your workspace name. A menu opens. Choose Settings, then Preferences. Notion's account settings help page describes this route, so you can match it against your own screen.
menuPath: Down arrow next to workspace name
steps.tip: The layout can shift between versions. Match the words you see rather than the exact position.

steps.name: Turn on Open Notion links in browser
steps.text: In the Preferences panel, scroll to Desktop app settings. Find the switch named Open Notion links in browser and turn it on. From this point, Notion sends links to your browser instead of the Mac app. Leave this window open for the next step only if you need to check the other switch.
steps.tip: Notion's help pages label this toggle slightly differently in places. Use the wording in your app.

steps.name: Sign in to Notion on the web
steps.text: Open a browser tab and go to Notion. Sign in to the same account and workspace you use in the Mac app. The web setting lives in your account preferences, not in the Mac app, so you need the web app open for the next step.

steps.name: Turn off Open links in desktop app
steps.text: In the web app, open Settings > Preferences. Find the switch named Open links in desktop app and turn it off. Now the two settings work as a pair. The desktop app sends links to the browser, and the web app stops sending links back into the Mac app.
steps.tip: If you turned this on earlier to get links into the Mac app, this is the switch that undoes it.

steps.name: Click a Notion link to test it
steps.text: Open an email, a chat, or a document that has a Notion link. Click it. A browser tab should open the page. If the Mac app opens instead, go back to steps 3 and 5 and check both switches. Then press ⌘R in the Mac app to refresh it and try a new link.
steps.tip: Notion's help lists ⌘R as the refresh shortcut on Mac. It does not change link routing.

shortcuts.action: Refresh the desktop client during the desktop beta

troubleshooting.problem: Links still open in the Mac app
troubleshooting.fix: Check both switches. In the Mac app, Open Notion links in browser must be on. In Notion on the web, Open links in desktop app must be off. Then press ⌘R in the Mac app and click a link you have not opened yet.

troubleshooting.problem: The Desktop beta toggle is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Notion's desktop beta page says to press ⌘⇧R on Mac to refresh the client. It refreshes the client, not the app itself. Beta needs app version 7.39.0 or later, so check your build first.
Quit the Notion desktop app and open it again. Then test a link from an email or a chat. Avoid changing the switches again until you have tested once, so you know which change made the difference.

troubleshooting.problem: Desktop app keeps launching by itself
troubleshooting.fix: Notion's help says device-level settings may override Notion settings. The steps on that page cover Windows only, so this guide has no verified Mac steps for it. Contact Notion support if the app keeps opening.
